title: Quasi-separated cancellation for a composite of stack morphisms
statement: Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme], universes [def-weil-size-convention], algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and the morphisms and $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of stack morphisms use [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal C$ morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$. Suppose $b\circ a$ is quasi-separated and the relative diagonal $\Delta_b:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$ is quasi-separated as a representable morphism, meaning that its algebraic-space scheme base changes have quasi-compact diagonals. Then $a$ is quasi-separated. Neither $a$ nor $b$ is assumed representable, quasi-compact or of finite type.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), clause (4), including its diagonal factorization and algebraic-space scheme tests.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ and $Q=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A$; these are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. There is a map $i:P\to Q$ sending $(x_1,x_2,\phi)$ to $(x_1,x_2,b(\phi))$, and $\Delta_{ba}\simeq i\Delta_a$. The map $i$ is a base change of $\Delta_b$ along $Q\to\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$, $(x_1,x_2,\psi)\mapsto(a(x_1),a(x_2),\psi)$. Indeed, a lift of this triple through $\Delta_b$ is precisely an isomorphism $\phi:a(x_1)\simeq a(x_2)$ satisfying $b(\phi)=\psi$: writing a lift as an object $y$ and isomorphisms $u:a(x_1)\simeq y$, $v:a(x_2)\simeq y$ gives $\phi=v^{-1}u$, with inverse $y=a(x_2),u=\phi,v=1$. These constructions respect arrows and pullbacks by the groupoid fibre-product formula [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Thus the square is $2$-cartesian. The representability assertion of [lem-sfb-stack-relative-diagonal-finite-type], applied to $a$ and $b$, makes $\Delta_a$ and $i$ representable by algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), proof of (4), diagonal factorization; Tag 050H (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), displayed 2-cartesian square, with its object-level verification written here; Tag 04XS (lemma-properties-diagonal), (1).

proof.text: Fix any scheme map $t:T\to P$ and use $it:T\to Q$ to form the algebraic spaces $E=\mathcal A\times_QT$ and $F=P\times_QT$, with maps $E\xrightarrow{u}F\xrightarrow{v}T$. The first space is the scheme test of $\Delta_{ba}$, and the second is the scheme test of $i$. By the square of step 1, $F\to T$ is also the scheme test of $\Delta_b$ at the composite $T\to Q\to\mathcal B\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$. Consequently $v$ is quasi-separated by the hypothesis on $\Delta_b$, while $vu:E\to T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the hypothesis on $ba$ and [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. These are assertions about these algebraic-space projections; they require no representability of $a$ or $b$.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), proof of (4), its algebraic spaces A and B (here E and F); Tag 04YW (definition-separated), (4).

proof.text: The map $u$ is quasi-separated by the following elementary diagonal calculation (the argument of Tag 03KR). Since $E,F,T$ are sheaves of sets [def-trf-algebraic-space], $j:E\times_FE\to E\times_TE$ is the inclusion of pairs having equal $F$-image. Pulling $\Delta_{E/T}$ back along $j$ gives exactly $\Delta_{E/F}$: a pair $(e_1,e_2)$ lies on either diagonal precisely when $e_1=e_2$, and then its two $F$-images agree automatically. The diagonal of $E\to T$ is quasi-compact by step 2 and [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Its pullback is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Hence $\Delta_{E/F}$ is quasi-compact, which is the algebraic-space definition of quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 03KR (lemma-compose-after-separated), (3), with the sheaf diagonal calculation written out; Tag 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-qc-cancellation] to the algebraic-space maps $E\xrightarrow{u}F\xrightarrow{v}T$. Its composite is quasi-compact by step 2, and $v$ is quasi-separated by that step, so $u$ is quasi-compact. The conventions agree as follows: [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] says that an algebraic space has quasi-compact point space exactly when it has a quasi-compact scheme atlas; [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] identifies quasi-compact morphisms with affine-scheme tests and gives stability under arbitrary algebraic-space base change. The stronger test by every quasi-compact algebraic space in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] implies the affine tests, and follows back from them: for a quasi-compact $Z\to Y$, the pullback $X\times_YZ\to Z$ is quasi-compact by base change, so applying its quasi-compact-scheme test to a quasi-compact scheme atlas $V\to Z$ gives a quasi-compact atlas of $X\times_YZ$. The composite of its etale atlas with the pullback of $V\to Z$ is etale and surjective, by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to these representable maps of algebraic spaces. Thus the output gives quasi-compactness in the statement's convention as well.

source.place: Tag 03KS (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), applied to E -> F -> T; Tag 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local), (1) iff (3); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), identifying the atlas and topological conventions.

proof.text: The original $t:T\to P$ gives a section $s:T\to F=P\times_QT$, $z\mapsto(t(z),z,1_{it(z)})$. Pulling $u:E\to F$ back along $s$ yields $H=\mathcal A\times_PT\to T$: in the iterated $2$-fibre product an object includes an identification of its $P$-coordinate with $t(z)$, so forgetting the redundant $Q$-coordinate gives this equivalence, with inverse inserting that coordinate and its identity isomorphism [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The map $H\to T$ is quasi-compact by step 4 and base-change stability [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Its diagonal is the base change of $\Delta_u$ along $H\times_TH\to E\times_FE$: both fibre products parametrize pairs of $E$-sections with the same $F$-image, together with their common $T$-coordinate. Hence that diagonal is quasi-compact by step 3 and the same base-change result, so $H\to T$ is quasi-separated. Step 1 supplies representability of $\Delta_a$; since $t$ was an arbitrary scheme test, [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] now says exactly that $a$ is quasi-separated.
